summary: Challenge to the constitutional validity of provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), particularly concerning attachment and confiscation of property, bail conditions, and reverse burden of proof; court upheld the validity of the provisions, applying the doctrine of proportionality and affirming the legislative intent to combat money laundering and maintain economic sovereignty.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 21 of the Constitution of India
Article 14 of the Constitution of India
M/s. Kartikeya Sharma v. Union of India
final_judgment: The petitions were dismissed, and the constitutional validity of the impugned provisions of the PMLA was upheld.
